newsitem.title: THAILAND: Outlook remains bleak for Thai steel industry.
newsitem.headline: Outlook remains bleak for Thai steel industry.

text.p: A near-term recovery for Thailand's battered steel industry is out of question as long as the country's economic slowdown drags on, analysts said.
A construction slump, spurred primarily by overbuilding, is likely to continue for at least two more years, analysts said.
"Until the economy picks up and the property glut improves, the steel producers will continue to face tough time ahead," said Chai Techakumpuch, an analyst at Vickers Ballas.

Sahaviriya Steel Industry Plc, the country's only hot-rolled coil producer, reported on Wednesday a net loss of 435.93 million baht ($17.77 million) during the first quarter compared with a loss of 111.17 million during the same period last year.
N.T.S. Steel, a major producer of steel bars and wire rods, lost 222.60 million baht compared with a profit of 959 million baht during the same period last year.
N.T.S. attributed the reversal to the sluggish economy and foreign exchange losses.
Uncompetitive prices for local steel have also squeezed Thai steelmakers.
Some local products were pressured by imports while others could not be exported in large quantities because they cannot be priced competitively in world markets.
"Thai steel makers, and in most cases steel makers in Southeast Asia, are just not competitive on the global basis to start with," said Eric Henderson of ING Barings.

"It is a relatively new industry here..Thailand does not have iron ore deposits. To transport that (into Thailand) is quite costly. Even if we do get economies of scale and develop the industry, it is still a bit of a disadvantage," he added.
N.T.S. Steel, for example, faced tough competition from lower-cost eastern bloc steel bar producers. Its products are around 20 percent more expensive than imports.
The slow economy has caused a surplus in steel bars with local supplies expected to outstrip demand by at least 300,000 tonnes this year, according to Vickers Ballas.
N.T.S. also faces higher interest expenses from 1997 to 1999 as it repays a loan for a new, re-rolling production line.
Vickers Ballas forecasts that. with its interest burden likely to worsen, N.T.S. will lose about one billion baht a year between 1997 and 1999.
ING Barings' Henderson forecast that Sahaviriya Steel's net loss for 1997 will be 1.05 billion baht compared with a loss of 1.7 billion baht in 1996.

Although the company received protection from the government in the form of anti-dumping duties imposed on imported hot-rolled coil and structural steel, the benefit failed to show in its January-March performance.

Moreover, the anti-dumping duties of between 25.29-51.90 percent, imposed in December, were preliminary. Final findings which are expected within the second quarter could reverse the decision, once again pressuring steel prices.
"If the anti-dumping tariff and improved margin failed to help, I don't expect any significant change in term of earning for Sahaviriya for the rest of the year," Henderson said. ($1 = 26 baht)
